messages:
devops-bot: [ALERT] apiserver latency spike in eu-west1 — 95th p90->p99 jump, error 502s increasing, correlated with NAT SNAT exhaustion on nat-gw-eu-2 :rotating_light:
alice.sre: seeing same in dashboards, apiserver request queue depth climbing, controller-manager reconcile delays are spiking
luis.infra: digging into VPC NAT metrics — conntrack table at 98% on nat-gw-eu-2, SNAT port usage near limit for several nodes
anya.eng: that would explain failed webhook calls and some list/watch errors we saw, GPUs provisioning stuck in Pending with attach timeouts
jon.prod: rolling alert for customer-facing failures? any impact to hosted API?
alice.sre: hosted API in other regions ok, but Dedicated pools in eu-west1 have ~20% fewer ready GPUs, some jobs stuck in ContainerCreating (AttachVolume timed out)
sre-oncall: I can try bumping kube-apiserver replicas and QPS settings while infra reduces source NAT pressure
luis.infra: trying a quick mitigation: increasing NAT ephemeral port range on nat-gw-eu-2 and rotating the NAT instance to new IP — will cause short egress blips
anya.eng: can we avoid a full rotate? rotate might drop active connections and make controller managers time out more
alice.sre: agree, do a gradual add: spawn secondary NAT gateway and start re-routing subset of subnets to it
luis.infra: started provisioning nat-gw-eu-3, will attach to same public IP pool once ready
devops-bot: deploy started: terraform apply plan-2026-03-21-002 — creating nat-gw-eu-3
/shell
luis.infra: quick check output:
```
$ ssh nat-gw-eu-2
# cat /proc/net/nf_conntrack | wc -l
235420
# sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max
262144
```
looks close to limit
anya.eng: controller log snippet — watch reconnects and 504s:
```
I0321 10:12:04.123 controller.go:256] error syncing "gpu-pool-asia": Post "https://apiserver.internal/apis/apps/v1/namespaces/infra/deployments": net/http: request canceled (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)
```
jon.prod: customer impact: a handful of Dedicated customers reported slow scaling ops, no data plane downtime reported yet
alice.sre: mitigation steps being applied: 1) add nat-gw-eu-3 and transition 30% of subnets 2) increase nf_conntrack_max to 400k on nat-gw-eu-2 as stopgap 3) temporarily relax apiserver leader-election and controller-manager QPS backoff thresholds
sre-oncall: I'm going to scale kube-apiserver to 5 replicas (from 3) in eu-west1 to help absorb retries — will do canary first
anya.eng: also lowering controller-manager --min-resync-period to reduce immediate retry storms? might help but careful on churn
luis.infra: nat-gw-eu-3 up and healthy, re-routing 30% of subnets now (doing small batches)
/devops-bot
devops-bot: route-update: subnets 10.12.0.0/16 10.13.0.0/16 moved to nat-gw-eu-3
luis.infra: conntrack on nat-gw-eu-2 dropping to ~160k after move, ephemeral port usage falling :thumbsup:
alice.sre: apiserver p99 latency trending down from 1.8s -> 320ms, controller-manager reconcile backlog decreasing
anya.eng: GPUs that were Pending started moving again, attach times back to normal on a few nodes
jon.prod: monitoring shows some customer autoscale retries resolved, posting update to status page in 15m
sre-oncall: scaled apiserver canary to 5 replicas; no new leader flaps observed. leaving config rollback window open for 30m
luis.infra: as permanent fix we'll: increase NAT pool size, distribute egress across additional NAT CGWs, and implement conntrack autoscale alerting
alice.sre: action items for postmortem: - root cause writeup (conntrack saturation from high ephemeral connections during large ephemeral external calls), - why autoscaling didn't trigger earlier, - tighten controller-manager backoff policies to avoid eliciting high fanout, - cost tradeoffs for larger NAT pool vs. transient scaleups
anya.eng: also capture what triggered the connection spike — looks like a burst of external model-downloads from dedicated onboarding jobs around 09:40 UTC
jon.prod: good, I'll coordinate customer comms and pricing/credits if any customers hit provisioning failures
/devops-bot
devops-bot: incident resolved (mitigated). incident id INC-2026-314 applied
alice.sre: creating PagerDuty follow-up and assigning to infra + controller-manager owners
luis.infra: posting terraform diff to the ops channel for review — PR coming
anya.eng: will add a small regression test to our rollout that simulates heavy egress during gpu attach to ensure conntrack thresholds observed in CI
sre-oncall: thanks all — leaving thread open for doc notes, but marking as mitigated for now :white_check_mark:
